title: Exploring Diffusion Models' Corruption Stage in Few-Shot Fine-tuning and Mitigating with Bayesian Neural Networks

problem.claim: Few-shot fine-tuning of diffusion models can exhibit a corruption stage in which image fidelity deteriorates and noisy patterns emerge before later recovery with severe overfitting.

gap.claim: The training dynamics and underlying cause of this corruption stage require explanation and mitigation.

contributions.claim: The authors identify and term the stage involving generated noisy patterns during few-shot fine-tuning the corruption stage.

The authors heuristically model one-shot fine-tuning, extend the modeling to more general cases, and attribute the corruption stage primarily to a narrowed learning distribution inherent in few-shot fine-tuning.

The authors apply Bayesian neural networks with variational inference to diffusion models to implicitly broaden the learned distribution, with a learning target described as an expectation of the diffusion loss plus regularization using pretrained diffusion models.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The approach is reported to be compatible with current few-shot fine-tuning methods and to introduce no additional inference costs.
Experiments are reported to significantly mitigate corruption and improve generated-image fidelity, quality, and diversity in object-driven and subject-driven generation tasks.

narrative_sequence.summary: Few-shot fine-tuning of diffusion models reduces training costs and enables personalized AI applications.
Training dynamics show a corruption stage in which fidelity deteriorates and noisy patterns emerge before later recovery accompanied by severe overfitting.
The authors model one-shot fine-tuning and generalize the modeling to explain the corruption stage as arising primarily from a narrowed learning distribution.
Bayesian neural networks with variational inference are applied to implicitly broaden the learned distribution through an expectation-based diffusion-loss target with pretrained-model regularization.
The method is reported to preserve compatibility and inference cost while improving corruption mitigation and image-generation metrics across two task settings.

source_observation.claim: Few-shot fine-tuning may narrow the learned distribution and produce a transient corruption stage with noisy outputs.

interpretation.claim: Monitoring training dynamics and distribution breadth may be important when adapting generative models from very limited data.

application.claim: Use training-stage monitoring and consider distribution-broadening regularization when developing few-shot generative-model fine-tuning workflows.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the same corruption mechanism or mitigation applies across datasets, architectures, or fine-tuning regimes beyond the reported settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, model architectures, baselines, or quantitative effect sizes.
The abstract does not provide details of the variational-inference implementation or regularization strength.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported experimental results.
